title: Payoff buckets: latency vs cost scan (annotated)
content:
Context:
This is a working sketch to map candidate SLO buckets (Gold/Silver/Bronze) to concrete runtime configurations and rough unit economics. Purpose: give PMs + SREs a short, actionable table to pick defaults for rollout experiments. Not final; contains rough approximations and open questions.

Summary (one line):
- For conversational workloads with median request length ~150 tokens and session prepends ~80 tokens, we see three distinct payoff regions where different knobs dominate: caching/prefix hit, quantized model variants, and tiling/prefetch (sessionized) gains.

Measurement setup (short):
- Cluster: dedicated A100-p4d-like (approx 1.2x baseline) and private V100 pool for replication.
- Models: base (FP16, 16B), quant-3 (4-bit hybrid), compact (8B distill).
- Workload: synthetic session mix derived from product traffic (70% chat single-turn, 30% mult-turn avg 5 turns).
- Key metric: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) per response generation end-to-end and $ cost normalized to $/1k tokens.
- Measurement note: network tail and client-side handshake excluded for pXX numbers; include total end-to-end in separate rows.

Text table (annotated):
Mode | Model | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k tokens | $/query@200t | Notes
-----|-------|---------:|--------:|--------:|-----------:|-------------:|------
Gold-fast | base-FP16 | 38 | 92 | 210 | 0.90 | 0.18 | low batching, aggressive prewarm slots
Gold-quant | quant-3 | 46 | 110 | 260 | 0.42 | 0.084 | 2.1x token cost reduction vs base; slight pXX penalty
Silver-prefetch | base-FP16+prefetch | 52 | 140 | 330 | 0.65 | 0.13 | prefix cache hitrate ~0.6 for sessions
Silver-compact | compact-8B | 60 | 170 | 430 | 0.28 | 0.056 | good for bursty low-latency tail control
Bronze-batch | base-FP16 (batched) | 120 | 400 | 900 | 0.20 | 0.04 | high batching; not suitable for interactive SLAs
Bronze-quant-batch | quant-3 (batched) | 160 | 520 | 1100 | 0.09 | 0.018 | cheapest but high latency tail
Private-onprem | base-FP16 (edge) | 48 | 120 | 290 | 0.75 | 0.15 | constrained networking; region-residency

Annotated takeaways:
- Quantization gives the largest $/token reduction (approx 2.0–2.5x) while incurring ~1.1–1.3x p90 and p99 penalties in microbursts. Good fit for Gold-quant and Bronze-quant-batch.
- Prefetch / prefix caching effectively shifts a portion of requests from Gold-fast to Silver-prefetch with modest $ savings; best when session re-use >50%. If session churn is high, gain disappears.
- Compact models (8B) reduce tail cost moderately while keeping p50 reasonable; they are a strong candidate for Silver tier where interactive tail penalty can be tolerated.
- Batching (Bronze) produces best $ numbers at the cost of long tails; use for background or non-interactive pipelines.

ASCII contour sketch (latency vs $/1k tokens):
(cheapest)  *---------------------------------------------* (expensive)
           |\\\\\  Bronze (batched)                  |
           | \\\\\ Bronze-quant                        |
           |  \\\\\ Silver-compact                   |
           |   \\\\\ Silver-prefetch                 |
           |    \\\\\ Gold-quant                       |
           |     \\\\\ Gold-fast                        |
Latency -> |      \\\\\                                    |
           |       *------------------------------------------*
             $/1k tokens -> cheaper ----------------------- more expensive

Note: vertical axis is latency (lower is better). The diagonal shows observed clusters when plotting p90 vs $/1k.

Micro-annotations and confidence:
- p50 figures have ±5% variance across three runs. p99 is noisy (±15%).
- Configs measured with steady-state load for 10 min windows; microburst tests show p99 can jump 2–3x briefly.
- Cost numbers include amortized GPU runtime + storage for KV cache but exclude networking egress.

Open questions / follow-ups:
1) Re-run on GA4 instance family (narrower GPU dim) to validate the quant-3 tail behavior — current cluster is A100-ish.
2) Add real traffic replay (customer topology) for one enterprise tenant to validate prefix hitrate assumptions.
3) Evaluate impact of longer prompts (median 400 tokens) on Gold vs Silver crossover point.
4) Tie these buckets to Console rollout presets — propose default knob set per bucket.

Proposed quick defaults (for experiment):
- Gold-fast: model=base-FP16, min_slots=2, prewarm=true, batch_window=1ms, kv_cache=false
- Gold-quant: model=quant-3, min_slots=1, prewarm=true, batch_window=1ms, kv_cache=false
- Silver-prefetch: model=base-FP16, prefetch_policy=session-prefix, kv_cache_ttl=120s, min_slots=0, batch_window=4ms
- Silver-compact: model=compact-8B, min_slots=0, batch_window=2ms, kv_cache=false
- Bronze: model=quant-3, batching=true, batch_window=40ms, min_slots=0, prewarm=false

Action items (owner):
- Asha: run GA4 repeat + add per-tenant replay (ETA 2w)
- Lars: instrument session-prefix hitrate diagnostic (ETA 1w)
- Maya: draft Console preset UI copy and rollout gating criteria (ETA 1w)

Notes-to-self: short-recording of reasoning for selection logic above — prefer quantized Gold when cost pressure >30% and predictable tail fallback policy is enabled (fallback to compact).
